question:
A 41-year-old asymptomatic woman attends her annual evaluation. Her 10-year risk of atherosclerotic
cardiovascular disease is calculated to be 15%, and her physician advises starting rosuvastatin and
low-dose aspirin. The patient mentions that her husband was recently diagnosed with *Helicobacter
pylori* infection via a urease breath test and is undergoing treatment. Concerned about the link
between *H. pylori* and gastric ulcers or cancer, she requests testing for *H. pylori*. What is the most

appropriate course of action regarding her request? Answer Choices: (A) Order serologic testing for H.
pylori antibodies (B) Order a stool culture for H. pylori (C) Recommend Helicobacter pylori antibody
serology testing (D) Recommend testing only if gastrointestinal symptoms develop (E) Recommend
empiric triple therapy without testing (F) Defer testing until after initiating aspirin therapy (G) Perform a
rapid urease test (H) Recommend a fecal antigen test for Helicobacter pylori infection (I) Schedule a
urea breath test in 4 weeks (J) Reassure the patient that Helicobacter pylori testing is unnecessary at
this time
 A. Defer testing until after initiating aspirin therapy
B. Recommend a fecal antigen test for Helicobacter pylori infection
C. Order serologic testing for H. pylori antibodies
D. Recommend Helicobacter pylori antibody serology testing
E. Reassure the patient that Helicobacter pylori testing is unnecessary at this time
F. Recommend empiric triple therapy without testing
G. Recommend testing only if gastrointestinal symptoms develop
H. Schedule a urea breath test in 4 weeks
I. Perform a rapid urease test
J. Order a stool culture for H. pylori
